not_measured_or_open: No BOUNDARY or SEAL evidence was generated: no Miri, ASan/MSan/TSan, dudect/ctgrind, FFI negative controls or caller-closure audit. This receipt is a FAST/BATCH downstream measurement, not a safety or cryptographic certificate.
The 808 families with no admitted recipe remain acquire-failure/no-recipe rows; they are SOURCE-UNREACHABLE, unchanged and unmeasured at every behavioural level.

dma, libssh and sslscan were attempted but did not reach L7 in this run; their rows record the measured outcome rather than the prior inherited grade. No retry was folded into the no-reuse atlas, because a targeted retry would have to reuse the other 189 rows and would no longer be a full no-reuse measurement.
The crate's own library test suite, cargo fmt and cargo clippy were not re-run in S42 (no src/ change was made).

No cross-candidate transcript-hash comparison was used as a regression signal: the before rows belong to the superseded candidate identity and an earlier harness, so their normalised hashes are not comparable. The measured level is the regression signal here.
The expansion container's documented writable host bind mount (/work) remains a standing infrastructure task; it was not changed or assessed in this subphase.
Constant-time behaviour of the S40 GCM tag comparison and the S39/S41 paths was not re-measured (no dudect/ctgrind run).
Network access was used for pristine-source acquisition (Debian pool, github.com, libssh.org); libssh.org was unreachable and github.com failed transiently, as recorded above.
non_claims: No family graduates to SAFE_COMPATIBLE in S42.
A fresh candidate-bound L7 count is not safety or cryptographic evidence (AGENTS.md section 8).

177 L7 of 192 recipe-backed families, 180 loaded, is a measurement of this candidate at e832606b7 under this venue; it is not a claim that the corpus is stable. Three previously measured families are infrastructure-limited in this run.
Zero candidate-only drops does not prove the three changes are behaviour-preserving; it establishes that none of the 192 admitted workloads observed a level regression attributable to the candidate.
